chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you fast, let your hearing, your vision, your hair, and your skin fast, and he enumerated other things besides this, and he said: 'The day of your fasting should not be like the day of your breaking (fasting)'.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean for the senses to 'fast' according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi expands the definition of fasting (Sawm) beyond mere dietary restriction to a holistic discipline of the senses and limbs, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the perfection of worship. The Imam’s instruction that the day of fasting should not differ from the day of Eid underscores the necessity of maintaining spiritual continuity and inner peace, ensuring that the physical abstinence translates into a sustained state of mindfulness (Taqwa).

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umey, from Hammad Bin usman, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whenever you Fast, so let your hearing, and your vision, and your hair, and your skin, and a number of this other than these, Fast (as well)’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The day of your Fast should not happen to be like the day of your breaking (not Fasting)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘When you fast, your ears, eyes, hairs and skin must also fast . . counting other things also, the Imam said that ‘the day of your fast should not be just like any other day.”’
